1.explanation: The distortion occurs in the WebGLPoints rendering pipeline when icons are rotated with the view and the viewport is not square. • WebGLPoints.js defines the layer and accepts the icon-rotate-with-view flag. • VectorStyleRenderer.js reads style properties (including rotation) and emits draw instructions for icon quads. • PointsLayer.js sets up the projection, resolution uniforms (width/height) and invokes the shader program to position and rotate each quad. • styleparser.js generates the GLSL code that applies icon rotation (with or without view) and maps pixel sizes into clip space. • Helper.js supplies the uniform data (resolution, viewRotation, rotateWithView) used by the shader. Together these files control how icon quads are transformed; the current code applies rotation before compensating for aspect ratio, leading to non-uniform scale. Adjusting the order of scale/rotate in styleparser or PointsLayer (and ensuring Helper writes correct uniform aspect factors) is required to fix the distortion.
1.bug_scenario: When using a WebGLPoints layer with “icon-rotate-with-view: true” on a non-square viewport, the icon quads are stretched or squashed instead of remaining square. In the reproducer the map container has unequal width/height and view.rotation = π/2, causing each icon to distort into a diamond-shape rather than a proper square. The distortion only appears when the viewport aspect ratio ≠ 1.

2.explanation:
All four files participate in handling and drawing rotated icons in the WebGLPoints layer.  
• WebGLPoints.js defines the layer, reads the “icon-rotate-with-view” style property, and chooses the PointsLayer renderer. It wires the high-level style option into the renderer.  
• PointsLayer.js (under renderer/webgl) initializes the WebGL program for points, passes the canvas resolution, rotation flags, and size uniforms to the shader. The distortion appears because the code here never compensates for non-square resolution when computing rotated offsets.  
• renderinstructions.js contains the GLSL snippet templates for POINTS—this is where the vertex positions for the icon quad are computed (rotation, offset, scale). The rotation math in the snippet assumes a square viewport and ignores the aspect ratio.  
• styleparser.js builds the style attributes and injects them into the shader over the buffers. It merges the rotate-with-view boolean into the generated program, but the transform it selects still doesn’t normalize by both width and height, so the icon’s x/y scaling is wrong when the viewport isn’t square.  
Together, these files control how rotated icons are passed to WebGL and rendered; fixing the distortion requires updating the rotation/offset logic and uniform handling in PointsLayer.js and renderinstructions.js (and possibly adjusting styleparser’s injected code) to use separate x/y resolution values when converting pixel offsets to clip space.
2.bug_scenario: When using a WebGLPoints layer with “icon-rotate-with-view: true” on a non-square viewport, the point icons are drawn squeezed or stretched rather than maintaining their correct aspect ratio. Rotating the map view still applies a rotation to the icon quad, but the rotation math and pixel->clip-space conversion don’t account for differing canvas width/height, so the icon gets distorted.
